bill.title: A joint resolution proposing an amendment to the Constitution of the United States relating to contributions and expenditures intended to affect elections.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on the Judiciary.

industries.rationale: Organizations that spend money to influence elections would face new potential restrictions on their expenditures and fundraising.
The amendment would create new constitutional authority to regulate campaign finance, directly affecting election law practice and lobbying activity.
Limits on campaign spending could affect demand for political advertising across broadcast, digital, and print media platforms.
The amendment's authorization to distinguish between natural persons and corporations could affect how financial institutions participate in election-related spending.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution proposes a constitutional amendment that would allow Congress and state governments to set limits on how much money candidates and others can raise and spend to influence elections. It would also permit lawmakers to treat corporations and other legal entities differently from individual people, including by prohibiting those entities from spending money on elections. The amendment would require ratification by three-fourths of the states to take effect.

bill.title: Family Farm and Small Business Exemption Act
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

industries.rationale: The bill directly exempts family farms from asset calculations for federal student aid eligibility.
The bill changes how federal student aid eligibility is calculated, affecting aid distribution and potentially enrollment patterns.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would restore an exemption that allows families to exclude the value of their farm or small business (with 100 or fewer employees) when applying for federal student aid. Recent changes to the financial aid application began counting these assets when determining how much aid a student qualifies for, starting in the 2024-2025 school year. The bill would return to the previous policy of not counting these family-owned farms and businesses as assets in the aid calculation.

plain.whoItTouches: Students, and people paying off a student loan. Students, and their families.

bill.title: National Plan for Epilepsy Act
bill.latestActionText: Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.

industries.rationale: The bill's focus on epilepsy treatment, diagnosis, and cure research directly affects pharmaceutical and medical device companies developing epilepsy therapies.
The national plan's coordination of epilepsy care and services would affect hospitals and health systems that diagnose and treat epilepsy patients.

bill.plainSummary: This bill directs the Department of Health and Human Services to create and carry out a national plan to address epilepsy, including prevention, diagnosis, treatment, and research coordination across federal agencies. HHS must establish an advisory council that reports to Congress every two years and must itself submit annual progress reports with recommended actions. These requirements would remain in effect until the end of 2035.

plain.whoItTouches: People with an illness that is still being studied. Anyone whose personal data is held by a company.

bill.title: Dolores River National Conservation Area and Special Management Area Act
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 480.

industries.rationale: The bill addresses livestock use within the conservation areas, which affects ranching operations on federal grazing allotments.
The conservation and special management area designations would likely restrict or prohibit new mining claims and mineral extraction on the designated federal lands.
Conservation area designations typically restrict or prohibit new energy development, potentially affecting oil and gas leasing rights on the affected federal lands.
The bill's focus on protecting recreational and scenic values may affect tourism and outdoor recreation businesses operating in or near the designated areas.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would create two protected areas along the Dolores River in Colorado: a 52,872-acre National Conservation Area on Bureau of Land Management land and a 15,452-acre Special Management Area in the San Juan National Forest. The bill requires management plans for both areas, preserves tribal access for traditional uses, prohibits road construction and motorized vehicles in the Ponderosa Gorge portion, and bars commercial timber harvesting there. It also establishes an advisory council and removes certain river segments from consideration for Wild and Scenic River designation.

plain.whoItTouches: Anyone who drives. People who live near or work on federal land.

The bill provides payments through fiscal year 2026, including back payments for 2024 and 2025, and allows counties and advisory committees to continue initiating projects through 2028.

bill.title: A joint resolution to direct the removal of United States Armed Forces from hostilities within or against Venezuela that have not been authorized by Congress.
bill.latestActionText: Point of order that the measure is not entitled to expedited procedures under 50 U.S.C. 1546(a) raised against the measure agreed to in Senate by Yea-Nay Vote. 50 - 50. Record Vote Number: 9.

industries.rationale: The resolution would directly affect the deployment and operational scope of U.S. Armed Forces and defense contractors supporting military operations in the Venezuela region.

bill.plainSummary: This joint resolution would require the President to end any U.S. military operations in or against Venezuela unless Congress has formally declared war or authorized the use of force. It preserves the President's authority to defend the United States from an armed attack or imminent threat. The measure addresses congressional oversight of military deployments and the constitutional division of war powers.

plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.

It reaffirms that supporting press freedom is a priority for U.S. foreign policy in promoting democracy and human rights. As a resolution, it does not change law or create new obligations; it is a formal statement of the Senate's position.

bill.title: A bill to prohibit the Secretary of the Interior from taking any action to expand the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry located near Glenwood Springs, Colorado.
bill.latestActionText: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.

industries.rationale: The bill directly prohibits expansion of a limestone quarry, affecting quarrying operations and materials extraction at that site.
Limestone quarries supply aggregate and materials for construction projects, so limiting this quarry's expansion could affect regional material supply.

bill.plainSummary: This bill would prevent the Secretary of the Interior from taking any action to expand a specific limestone quarry located near Glenwood Springs, Colorado. It targets one named facility, the Mid-Continent Limestone Quarry, and would block federal approval or support for any expansion of that operation. The bill does not address quarrying generally or other facilities.
